page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.1-2 is an ARM-based compute instance built on the Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 architecture. It provides 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) operating at 3.0 GHz, accompanied by 2.0 GB of system memory and hardware AES encryption support. The instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. It contains no bundled local storage or dedicated graphics processors, relying on network-attached storage for disk operations.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the single-core configuration. The instance recorded an average single-core stress-ng result of 1653.59, matching its multi-core output due to the single-thread allocation. Memory benchmarks showed read throughput of 12.51 GB/sec and write throughput of 7.99 GB/sec on large 256MB blocks, alongside a PassMark memory score of 736.74. Application tests demonstrated 1.32 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.12 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Overall throughput remains bounded by the single-core and 2.0 GB memory envelope.

Because the core is dedicated rather than shared or burstable, the instance avoids noisy-neighbor contention common in entry-tier virtual machines. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.1-2 is technically matched to low-intensity workloads, including lightweight web serving, microservices, edge orchestration agents, and development or testing environments requiring an arm64 execution target.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.1-2 is an entry-tier arm64 instance powered by a 3.0 GHz Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU), 2.0 GB of system memory, hardware-accelerated AES encryption, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server does not include local storage or GPU acceleration, depending on remote storage volumes for persistent data. In synthetic benchmarks, it achieves an average stress-ng single-core score of 1653.59, alongside 1.32 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.12 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, while multithreaded scalability is limited by its single-core configuration. The dedicated allocation ensures consistent execution without CPU scheduling contention. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.1-2 is suitable for low-overhead microservices, lightweight web servers, edge utilities, and basic software test environments.
